title: Laser tattoo removal
what: A laser breaks the ink in the skin into tiny particles, and the body slowly clears them away. The tattoo fades a little more with each session.
why: When you want to remove or lighten a tattoo, or permanent makeup on the brows or lips.
duration: a session usually takes 10 to 30 minutes; many sessions are often needed, spaced a few weeks apart
tell_doctor: Whether you have been in the sun recently
If you have had raised, thick scars (keloids)
All medicines, especially blood thinners and ones that make you sensitive to the sun

prepare.title: Sun
prepare.text: Do not sunbathe before the procedure. Ask the clinic for how long.

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: The skin over the tattoo should be clean, with no creams.

prepare.title: Pain relief
prepare.text: Sometimes numbing cream is applied beforehand. Ask the clinic.

prepare.title: Expectations
prepare.text: The doctor will say roughly how many sessions your tattoo needs.

bring: Comfortable clothes that uncover the tattoo
steps: The doctor examines the tattoo and the skin
The laser treats the tattoo in short flashes
A healing product and a dressing are applied
feel: It hurts, like snaps of a rubber band or splashes of hot oil
after: Redness, swelling, sometimes blisters and crusts usually pass in 1 to 2 weeks
No sauna or pool until the skin has healed
Use sunscreen on the area while the sessions continue
red_flags: Pus, growing pain, fever: see a doctor
The wound is slow to heal

faq.q: Can a tattoo be removed completely?
faq.a: Often yes, but not always. Colored and old tattoos respond differently. The doctor will tell you after an exam.
Usually not, if you care for the skin properly. The risk is higher with a tendency to raised scars.

reminders.text: Tattoo removal tomorrow. No sunbathing, and no creams on the skin.
